caption: Fast gates (tens of nanoseconds), fixed nearest-neighbor wiring, and a dilution refrigerator running near absolute zero.
Slower gates (microseconds), all-to-all connectivity within a chain, and a demanding laser/optics setup instead of extreme cold.

steps.label: Gate speed
steps.sub: ~50 ns vs. ~20 μs, illustratively — roughly 400x, order of magnitude 2-3

steps.label: Connectivity
steps.sub: Fixed neighbors + SWAP overhead vs. all-to-all within one chain

steps.label: Fidelity (illustrative)
steps.sub: ~99.5% vs. ~99.9% two-qubit — ion error rate roughly 5x lower in this example

eyebrow: Different bottlenecks, not the same one

steps.label: Superconducting
steps.sub: Wiring density and cryostat heat load as qubit count grows

steps.label: Trapped-ion
steps.sub: Laser engineering and chain-length limits from motional mode crowding

steps.label: No settled winner
steps.sub: Real, unresolved tradeoffs being made differently by different companies
